messages.subject: [statnet_help] involving covariates in ergm
messages.body_plain:
Dear list,

Thank  you very much for reading this email.

I have been trying to involve some individual covariates such as gender, age, marriage, etc, into the ERGM model. So far, the example I found about this topic usually use an existing network object with the covariates already in it. However, in my case, the data is still in the raw data file. So my question is:

1. By using ERGM package in the statnet suite, is it possible to have the adjacency matrix and the data of the covariates in the same raw data file? or should I put the data of the covariates in a seperate data file?

2. In R, I expect that the adjacency matrix can be read in either way, but how to read the data of the covariates into the network object? Is there any example I can check?

Thank you very much.

Best regards,

ya

messages.subject: [statnet_help] involving covariates in ergm
messages.body_plain:
I am no expert, but I have been reading my network and my network attributes separately. You have to make sure that the nodes in your adjacency matrix (or edgelist) are in the same order as in your node attributes file. 

then you use the %v% to set network attributes (look at the network package documentation). But it should be something like: 

net %v% "gender" <- var_with_nodes_values$gender

Juan

messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

I am having two issues, which I feel might be related.

Every time I run an ERGM with a dataset examining ties between states, I 
get the following error:

[1] "Warning:  This network contains loops"

This is even after specifying that there are no loops in the network at 
practically every step along the way.

Here's the relevant output:

matrix1994 <- read.csv("1994_matrix5.csv", header=F, stringsAsFactors=F, sep="\t")
matrix1994 <- as.matrix(matrix1994,supress.diag=T)
attr1994 <- read.csv("attr1994.csv", header=T, stringsAsFactors=F, sep="\t")
rownames(matrix1994) <- attr1994$state
colnames(matrix1994) <- attr1994$state
#Let's make this all into an edgelist
e1994 <- as.edgelist.sna(matrix1994)
net1994 <- network(e1994, directed=F, loops=F)
m0 <- ergm(net1994 ~ density, loops=F   )
[1] "Warning:  This network contains loops"


Additionally, depending on the data I use, I also get an error that NANs 
are produced.  I found a post by Mark Handcock regarding the Nan 
problem, in which he suggests entering missing values as NA instead of 0 
or 1.  The thing is, the data I have in a complete sample of all the 
states, there is actually no missing data.

> matrix1994 <- read.csv("1994_matrix.csv", header=F, stringsAsFactors=F, sep="\t")
> matrix1994 <- as.matrix(matrix1994,supress.diag=T)
> attr1994 <- read.csv("attr1994.csv", header=T, stringsAsFactors=F, sep="\t")

> #Let's make this all into an edgelist

> m0 <- ergm(net1994 ~ density, loops=F   )
[1] "Warning:  This network contains loops"
Warning message:
In log(Clist$nedges/(Clist$ndyads - Clist$nedges)) : NaNs produced


I have three datasets, 1994_matrix.csv, 1994_matrix5, and 1994_matrix7.  
They're all the same data, though the ones followed by a number have 
ties valued at less than that number set to zero (ie: if an edge is 
valued at less than 7 in 199_matrix.csv, it is valued at 0 in 
1994_matrix7.csv).

I've looked through the archives and Google and can't seem to find 
anything addressing these issues.  Does anyone have any ideas?

Thanks,

Shane

Can someone please help me with this query about the interpretation of terms in the rem.dyad model in relevent in R?

I am particularly interested in the distinction between this term:

PSAB-BA: P-Shift effect (turn receiving) ? AB->BA (dyadic)

And these two terms:

RRecSnd: Recency of receipt of actions from v? affects v?s future rate of sending to v?
RSndSnd: Recency of sending to v? affects v?s future rate of sending to v?

messages.subject: [statnet_help] rem.dyad terms in relevent in R
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] rem.dyad terms in relevent in R
messages.body_plain:
Hi, Mark.  You are indeed correct: the P-shift terms relate to the next 
event in the sequence, while the R* terms reflect overall recency in 
terms of events ever received (RRec) or sent (RSnd) by the focal actor.

The statistics associated with these terms are described formally in:

Butts, C.T. (2008). "A Relational Event Framework for Social Action."  
Sociological Methodology, 38(1), 155-200.

Note that, as a general matter, RRecSnd and PSAB-BA involve distinct 
types of reciprocity, and both can be active within the same exchange.  
The former reflects the tendency of ego to send to alters who have most 
recently directed events to him or her (relative to other alters who 
have directed events towards ego); this depends only on ego's incoming 
event history, and not on other activity within the event sequence.  By 
contrast, the latter reflects temporally local turn-taking dynamics (the 
tendency of the next event to be a response from the last receiver to 
the last sender), and is not egocentric in character.  If you are 
dealing with a small-group setting, you will probably find P-shift 
effects (including the AB-BA shift) to be quite important; in a setting 
where actions are not globally observable (e.g., email), such effects 
are typically contraindicated.

Hope that helps,

-Carter
